purpose: Decisive vertical test of whether support can be composed from reusable non-lexical factor interfaces without simulator semantic-label leakage.

semantic_target.claim_boundary: Operational evidence for a mechanical support episode/disposition. Not a universal lexical definition and not metaphysical proof.

simulation.dimensionality: 3D vectors with translational rigid-body dynamics; orientation fixed for v1 boxes
simulation.contact_model: unilateral normal spring-damper penalty force; no semantic support flag
simulation.supporter_motion: fixed except collapse episode where vertical compliance/failure is explicitly modeled

estimated_contact.rule: candidate boundary separation <= 0.001 m for at least 80% of the final 0.5 s observation window AND median normal contact force >= 0.5 N

gravity_relative_position.rule: projection of (upper_center - supporter_center) onto unit vector opposite gravity is positive and lateral projected footprint overlap is >= 0.5

normal_load_transfer.rule: median projection of contact force on unit vector opposite gravity over final 0.5 s >= 0.5 * upper_mass * |g|

bounded_relative_displacement.rule: upper-supporter relative displacement magnitude over final 0.5 s <= 0.01 m

sustained_load_response.note: No semantic support label is used.

supporter_removal_dependence.rule: paired counterfactual from identical pre-removal state: removing candidate supporter causes upper-body displacement along gravity >= 0.05 m within 0.5 s more than the supporter-present continuation
supporter_removal_dependence.role: Disposition/counterfactual evidence; not required for the episode-level static composition but required for support_disposition evidence.

semantic_composition.non_support_evidence: at least one required factor is confidently false and evidence is non-conflicting
semantic_composition.support_disposition_evidence: support_episode_evidence AND supporter_removal_dependence AND stable_support_under_increased_load episode passes

episodes.ground_truth_only: attachment state may define fixture physics but not inference

transformation_tests.coordinate_rotation: Apply deterministic proper rotations to every raw vector and position around a transformed origin; factor and semantic predictions must be unchanged.
transformation_tests.coordinate_translation: Translate all positions by the same vector; predictions unchanged.
transformation_tests.gravity_rotation: Rotate bodies, forces, velocities and gravity together; predictions unchanged.

decision_metrics: episode classification agreement with preregistered expectations
whether factor definitions require environment-specific changes
go_criteria: All 10 required episode families meet preregistered factor/semantic expectations or refuse only where the plan explicitly permits ambiguity.
Coordinate and gravity transformation tests preserve predictions.
Contact-only cases do not classify as support.
Stable increased-load and collapse episodes separate through load-response factors.
Supporter-removal counterfactual adds a measurable disposition signal.
A subsequent non-simulated adapter can instantiate the same factor interfaces without redefining them.
stop_or_narrow_criteria: Factor definitions must be rewritten for individual episode fixtures.
Transformation invariance fails under physically equivalent transformed states.
Load-response/counterfactual factors add no discriminative structure beyond fixture labels.
Cross-environment reuse later requires redefining factor semantics rather than adapting measurements.
versioning: Any material rule/tolerance/episode change after implementation results requires simulation_plan_v2.json; v1 is retained.
